message.content: In Christian theology, Jesus Christ is regarded as the central and ultimate figure—often described as the fulfillment of the prophetic tradition. However, many Christians also hold the prophets of the Hebrew Scriptures (such as Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and others) in high esteem for their foundational role in shaping the narrative that leads to Jesus. Thus, while Jesus is typically seen as the most pivotal figure in Christianity, the prophets of the Old Testament are also considered essential to the faith’s history and teachings.
